To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the supersaturation in the wetting layer is the driving force for the formation of NDs, ND-molecules, and NWs; (ii) the supersatuation is determined by the deposition rate, the growth temperature, and the lattice mismatch; (iii) the supersatuated wetting layer can be consumed abruptly and the resulting NDs exhibit a homogeneous size distribution; (iv) the supersaturated wetting layer allows the formation of perfectly site-controlled and highly ordered NDs
the growth of NDs and NWs from supersaturated Ge WLs on Si(001) can be controlled by the growth temperature and the Ge flux.
the growth of NDs, ND-molecules, and NWs is driven by elastic energy relaxation, and the formation of these nanostructures is strongly influenced by the supersaturated WL.

the fundamental understanding of the growth mechanisms of nanostructures in epitaxial semiconductor material systems.
the understanding of the formation of nanostructure arrays from the supersaturated wetting layer.
the fundamental understanding of epitaxial growth phenomena, which is essential for the controlled fabrication of nanostructure-based devices.

the epitaxial growth of nanostructures in a supersaturated WL is a highly complex process, which can be understood and controlled only by considering all relevant physical parameters.
the supersatuated WL is a crucial element in the formation of NDs and NWs in lattice-mismatch systems.
the supersatuated WL is a key player for the formation and growth of NDs and NWs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
epitaxial semiconductor NDs and NWs can be obtained in a wide range of lattice-mismatched semiconductor heterostructures by a careful control of the growth parameters.
the careful control of supersaturation and growth temperature in lattice-mismatch systems allows us to obtain a broad spectrum of ND- and NW-based nanostructures with a high degree of perfection.
the careful control of material deposition and growth parameters allows us to tailor the growth of epitaxially strained nanostructures in a deterministic way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the supersatuation of the WL, which is often neglected in growth models, is the crucial parameter to control the formation of NDs, ND-molecules and NWs.
a careful control of supersaturation of epitaxial layers is a promising way to design and grow nanostructures with a high degree of perfection and control.
supersaturation of wetting layers can be used to control and tune the formation of epitaxial nanostructures in a wide variety of systems.
